model.description: MODEL_EXTRACTOR — REQUIRED, no default: a model default in code is how a run silently measures a different model than the report claims (P5 finding)

provider_extra.description: The provider overlay of this cell. Its one knob is the deliberation budget at provider_extra.reasoning.effort (MEMORY_REASONING_EXTRACT) — set explicitly, never inherited from the provider default. Declared as the overlay rather than as the flat `reasoning_effort` param because the overlay is applied last and wins over that param anyway; a setting named after the flat param would name a field this cell does not set.

description.purpose: Turns one accumulated batch of raw turns into structured facts, entities and edges. Deliberately the cheap model tier — benchmarks show extraction is not the quality bottleneck, retrieval and read-time reasoning are.
description.use_when: Called by extract-glue exactly once per claimed batch (~128 accumulated tokens or a 2-minute-old item by default), never per message.
description.not_in_scope: No validation (extract-glue never trusts this output), no store access, no consolidation reasoning — that is the dreamer's expensive tier. No conversation metadata either: that a turn was asked, answered or discussed is never a fact (O-6) -- the discipline lives in the prompt that extract-glue sends, not in this cell.
description.emits_meaning: messages[]: one assistant turn holding the extraction JSON. hop.finish_reason='error' is not a crash: extract-glue hands the batch back to the queue and the next gate retries it.
description.consumes_meaning: system.instructions.text: the extraction contract (JSON shape, fact_kind semantics). messages[]: one user turn with the batch items as JSON.
examples: a question turn ("which editors did I prefer in the last 7 days?") and the assistant's answer to it -> {"facts":[],"entities":[],"edges":[]}: the conversation is the episode, the world state is unchanged (O-6)
